tpitabs.name: Agent Rhy · APAC MI Pack consolidation (RHY)

rows.t: Agent Rhy reads all site MI Packs and drafts the APAC consolidation
rows.act: Agent reads the 9 site packs in SharePoint and drafts regional commentary. Baseline 31 hours a month; 9.5 hours delivered.

rows.t: Site-level insight on demand
rows.act: Ask Rhy for the key points per site, e.g. two executive summary points per site for the month, with source citations.

rows.t: Driver-based output in one fixed structure
rows.act: One line per driver: site, Fav/Adv, $m, driver. Grouped by COGM, variable, fixed, other cost, FTE and capex; top 1–4 per category.

rows.t: Timing versus structural tag on every driver
rows.act: The instruction set classes each driver as timing or structural, so the forecast impact is visible in the commentary.

rows.t: Agent Charlie for APAC planning pack consolidation
rows.act: Same approach for planning packs, in testing during the MTP cycle. Gives a regional headline by cost category.

rows.t: Site concise summary and cheat sheet for site reviews
rows.act: Charlie gives a three-point summary per site with risks and opportunities, focused on the 20% of insights that matter.

rows.t: Riff agent for slide-specific comments across site decks
rows.act: Consolidates one named slide, e.g. Direct & Indirect Split, across all site packs into a regional headline.

rows.t: Keep business judgement as the final review step
rows.act: Analysts validate and refine every draft. The deck shows a wrong Wuxi capex driver corrected only after a challenge.

rows.t: Stabilise the agent before relying on it in close
rows.act: Stable in 3 of 7 test months. Issues: instructions ignored, missing site, usage limit, unknown errors, prior-month carry-over.

rows.t: Protect capacity for testing, refinement and upskilling
rows.act: 6 of the 9.5 hours saved each month are reinvested in learning and optimisation. Net gain is about 11%.

rows.t: Completeness check before the agent runs
rows.act: Power Automate lists the files found against the 9 in-scope sites and stops the run if a pack is missing or still in draft.

rows.t: Extract the numbers with Python, let the agent write the words
rows.act: Pull variance values by rule, not by the model. The agent then explains drivers only, which removes most accuracy rework.

rows.t: Tie agent totals back to the Ops P&L report
rows.act: Compare each category total with the Ops P&L Power BI figures and flag any gap before the draft is shared.

rows.t: Use the Site Cost & FTE dashboard as the source for cost and FTE numbers
rows.act: The July dashboard already holds governed site cost and FTE data. Rhy can cite it instead of reading values from slides.

rows.t: Period and version guard on the knowledge hub
rows.act: Check month and Final/Draft status on each file before reading, and archive old months so prior commentary cannot carry over.

rows.t: Trigger the run when final packs land
rows.act: Power Automate starts Rhy once all final site packs are in the folder and posts the draft to Teams. No manual prompting.

rows.t: Store the driver output as a monthly table
rows.act: Save site, category, value, direction, driver and timing tag each month. Power BI then shows the variance bridge and repeat drivers.

rows.t: Consolidated APAC risks and opportunities view
rows.act: Roll up each site's R&O table (likelihood, timing, $m) into one regional list. North Ryde alone shows $1.7m up, $2.2m down.

rows.t: Golden test month for regression testing
rows.act: Rerun one validated month after every instruction or model change and compare with the approved commentary.

rows.t: Version-controlled prompt and instruction library
rows.act: Hold the Rhy, Charlie and Riff instructions and standard prompts per comparator in one place with change history.

rows.t: Run log, correction tracker and fallback route
rows.act: Log each run, error and analyst correction in a SharePoint list, and agree the manual path for months the agent is down.

rows.t: Volume commentary pulled forward to WD+1 with Global Supply Chain
rows.act: GFS sends key brands to NSP on WD-4. NSP inputs by end WD-1, GFS picks up on WD+1 AM and drafts for site finance on WD+2.

A like-for-like comparison between Actuals and Planning may be challenging with the current dataset for the following reasons:
1. Different levels of granularity: Actuals are available at the general ledger (GL) level, whereas Planning data is maintained at a higher level, such as the WRAP level.
2. Planning assumptions are not captured: The underlying assumptions used for the Planning figures are not currently stored in the dashboard, which limits the ability to explain or reconcile variances.

Reviewed and aligned with further input
